tweet_summary: Tweet says 'A US citizen was fined $130 for not having their papers on them. Tell me this isn't Germany again', over a video about Chicago man Ruben Cruz being fined by ICE for not carrying his immigration documents.
why_note_decision: The tweet's headline claim is false in a specific, checkable way: the man fined (Ruben Antonio Cruz, ~60, from El Salvador) is a lawful PERMANENT RESIDENT (green-card holder), NOT a U.S. citizen. This distinction is legally material: federal law (8 USC 1304(e)) requires non-citizens 18+ to carry their registration/green card at all times, while U.S. citizens have no such requirement. The tweet's own video correctly identifies Cruz as a legal permanent resident; the tweet text mislabels him 'a US citizen', which inverts the legal facts and inflates the claim. A note correcting the citizen-vs-LPR error is warranted. Provisional 'no_note' is wrong — there is a concrete false factual claim.
judge_guidance: A correct note must establish that the person fined is a lawful permanent resident (green-card holder), NOT a U.S. citizen, and that under federal law (8 USC 1304(e)) non-citizens 18+ must carry their registration document while U.S. citizens are not required to. It must AVOID the original note's drift into citing newsbreak.com (a low-trust aggregator, flagged SourcesMissingOrUnreliable). PASS if the note corrects the citizen/LPR mischaracterization with a reliable source (NBC Chicago or the U.S. Code) and notes the carry requirement applies to non-citizens; FAIL if it (a) accepts the 'US citizen' framing, (b) claims citizens must carry papers, or (c) relies solely on an unreliable aggregator. A bare 'note not needed' should FAIL — the false 'US citizen' claim is the whole point of the tweet.
reference_note: The man fined was a lawful permanent resident (green-card holder), not a U.S. citizen. original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substance is correct (LPR not citizen; carry requirement), but it cited a newsbreak.com re-host instead of the primary NBC Chicago report — heavily downrated SourcesMissingOrUnreliable (4) and MissingKeyPoints (8). A correct note keeps the same facts but cites the primary outlet and the U.S. Code directly.

fact_check.claim_verdict: False: subject is a lawful permanent resident, not a U.S. citizen; carry requirement applies to non-citizens.
fact_check.notes: Ruben Antonio Cruz, ~60, originally El Salvador, lawful permanent resident, fined $130 in Rogers Park, Chicago (Oct 9). 8 USC 1304(e) requires non-citizens 18+ to carry registration (fine up to $100); citizens have no such obligation. Experts note the law was historically rarely enforced.

importance.lens_rationale: Immigration-enforcement reach is a meaningful civil-liberties topic; correcting the citizen/LPR conflation prevents both inflated fear and dismissive backlash, modest societal value.
